title: Streaming stable boundaries and toolcall replay contract
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: when long streaming responses contain structured outputs (JSONL or explicit function/tool call events), clients that disconnect and reconnect can end up with broken JSON boundaries or duplicate tool invocations. Legacy clients and intermediary proxies further complicate framing because they may re-chunk SSE frames or collapse adjacent events.

Goal: define a server-client contract and server-side behavior that lets clients resume streams deterministically while preserving function-call boundaries and structured output parseability, without introducing a breaking change for older clients. The contract should be efficient (compact resume tokens), forensic-friendly (replayable), and compatible with HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 environments.

Proposal summary:
- Emit periodic opaque resume tokens as a special 'checkpoint' SSE event. Tokens encode minimal state: stream_id, seq_num, byte_offset, checksum, framing_version.
- Introduce a lightweight sentinel event type ('checkpoint') that marks canonical boundaries (every N tokens or at toolcall/JSONL record end).
- For structured outputs and tool/function calls, include a length-prefixed envelope inside the SSE data payload so proxies that coalesce events can still reconstruct record boundaries.
- Server-side dedupe: attach a per-toolcall id and maintain a short-lived dedupe store (24h) to prevent double-execution when clients accidentally replay the last partial chunk.
- Compatibility mode: servers continue to support legacy-framing when clients don't provide a resume token or advertise framing_version=0. SDKs will default to framing_version=1 after migration period.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can resume streams without losing function-call boundaries or producing duplicate function calls
Resume tokens are stable across retries and survive proxy buffering
Structured JSONL output remains parseable after reconnect across all official SDKs
No breaking change for legacy / pre-compat clients — server falls back to legacy-framing mode
tech_notes: Introduce 'resume_token' field serialized as base64-encoded checkpoint: { stream_id, seq_num, byte_offset, checksum, framing_version }
Use 'sentinel' event type with monotonic 'checkpoint' numbers emitted every N tokens or at toolcall boundaries
Implement server-side idempotency for toolcall invocations: attach per-toolcall id and at-least-once semantics converted to at-most-once via dedupe store for 24h
Batching-level and chunking heuristics: prefer semantic boundaries (sentences, JSON delimiters) over fixed byte windows when latency SLO allows
decisions: Opted for explicit framing_version to enable future rollouts without client changes
Favor compact resume tokens rather than long snapshots to avoid leaking prompt content
Require SDKs to expose resume+replay helpers; server will accept either token or (stream_id, last_seq) tuple for compatibility
migration_plan: 1) Deploy minimal framing_version=1 to internal canary with SDK instrumentation
2) Run A/B: 5% traffic using new framing vs legacy; collect parse error/regression metrics
3) Enable dedupe store and slow rollout to 100% with a week-long monitoring window
4) Publish SDK updates and migration guide
risks: Clients that buffer raw bytes may split JSON boundaries incorrectly after reconnect
Proxies that re-chunk SSE may invalidate resume token heuristics; mitigation: shorten checkpoint windows and emit sentinel events more frequently
Dedupe store introduces stateful component with cost; need eviction policy
